requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority on node1 named “OS Comparison Root CA” and install its certificate as a trusted system certificate authority.
requirements.summary: The self-signed certificate has the exact requested common name, CA:TRUE constraints, and a matching root-owned private key. It is registered through the legacy system CA configuration and trust bundle. Certificates issued by it verified successfully through both the explicit system bundle and the default trust path before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remained unchanged across execution and reboot. OpenSSL and ca-certificates were installed from the configured Gutsy archive, and their trust tooling worked on the platform.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, the restart was acknowledged and bounded downtime observed, a different boot identity appeared, and CA trust, key persistence, networking, and SSH health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Systemd service-failure inspection was unsupported on this legacy release, limiting broad failed-service hygiene assessment.
The lifecycle collector did not independently inventory the trust store; trust persistence is established by detailed executor commands instead.
Installed packages were reported by apt as unauthenticated, although they came from the preconfigured Ubuntu Gutsy archive and functioned successfully.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package-index refresh and package installation were necessary prerequisites (cmd-87d545d91c084a20, cmd-05bdc8db3a6d4883); CA generation and native trust registration directly implemented the outcome (cmd-e7ab19441dc14cdc, cmd-cdd5f673e5664798); temporary verification artifacts were bounded and cleaned (cmd-b80880241e364229, cmd-c3f26973cae04189, cmd-903e3e91bcf6449f); and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-c75c47fa62f749f3). Final snapshots show no temporary-file residue or package inconsistency. The deduction reflects installation of packages that apt explicitly reported as unauthenticated from HTTP-based legacy repositories, leaving a supply-chain hygiene concern despite their task relevance.
